D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 covers the full AI Engineer stack end-to-end: advanced Python engineering, classical ML, deep learning, NLP/Transformers, RAG, MLOps (Docker, FastAPI, MLflow), and cloud deployment on AWS — all tied to a single progressive capstone that is deployed and demo-ready. Interview prep is woven throughout all 12 weeks with explicit LeetCode progression, SQL milestones, ML system design, and behavioral STAR practice. Plan 2 covers similar technical breadth but at a shallower depth per topic, and its capstone is only initiated in Week 11 and completed in Week 12, leaving almost no time for polish or deployment. Plan 2's interview prep is largely deferred to the final week, which is a significant structural weakness for hiring readiness. Plan 1's portfolio artifact — a deployed Dockerized FastAPI app with Streamlit UI, MLflow tracking, and cloud hosting — is substantially more employer-worthy than Plan 2's less-defined capstone. Plan 2 does include useful resources and Kaggle practice but lacks the deployment depth and interview integration that AI Engineer roles globally demand.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 1 delivers a fully deployed, documented capstone with consistent interview prep across all 12 weeks, versus Plan 2's last-minute capstone and deferred interview preparation.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 explicitly accounts for 388 planned hours out of 432 available, with 44 buffer hours — a well-structured allocation. It breaks down monthly hours into theory, practice, and project work. However, some weeks in Plan 1 are ambitious: Week 9 covers NLP fine-tuning, RAG, and AWS setup simultaneously, which is cognitively dense. Plan 2 provides a daily breakdown (1.5h theory, 2.5h coding, 1h project, 0.5h review, 0.5h networking) but does not explicitly track total hours or buffer. Plan 2's weekly topic lists are also very dense — Week 8 covers text preprocessing, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, attention, transformers, and NLP applications in one week, which is unrealistic for 42 hours. Both plans have some overloading, but Plan 1's explicit hour accounting and buffer planning give it a structural advantage. Plan 2's final two weeks trying to complete a capstone, build a portfolio, optimize LinkedIn, and do interview prep simultaneously is a feasibility concern.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 1 explicitly tracks hours with a 44-hour buffer and distributes project work progressively, while Plan 2 has no hour accounting and compresses capstone, portfolio, and interview prep into the final two weeks.
